overview.title: Why consider OpenPanel over Mixpanel?
paragraphs: Mixpanel is one of the most established product analytics platforms, used by product teams worldwide to track user behavior, build funnels, and analyze retention. It's powerful, but that power comes with increasingly complex pricing, a cloud-only architecture, and cookie-based tracking that creates friction for privacy-conscious teams.

OpenPanel provides the core product analytics features most teams actually use, events, funnels, retention, cohorts, and user profiles, in a simpler package with transparent, predictable pricing. Starting at just $2.50 per month, or completely free when self-hosted, OpenPanel is dramatically more affordable than Mixpanel's pricing which can scale to thousands per month as your event volume grows.

Privacy is where the two platforms diverge most sharply. Mixpanel uses cookies by default and stores data on US servers, which means GDPR consent banners and data transfer concerns for European users. OpenPanel is cookie-free by default with EU-only hosting, making compliance straightforward. You can also self-host OpenPanel on your own infrastructure for complete data sovereignty, something Mixpanel simply doesn't offer.

For teams that want Mixpanel-style product analytics without the enterprise pricing, vendor lock-in, or privacy trade-offs, OpenPanel is a compelling open-source alternative that gives you full ownership of your analytics data.

feature_comparison.title: Feature comparison
feature_comparison.intro: OpenPanel covers the core analytics most teams need, while Mixpanel extends into enterprise-grade experimentation and session replay.

features.name: Funnels
features.notes: Mixpanel offers more advanced multi-path funnels

features.name: Cohorts
features.notes: Mixpanel has more advanced cohort builder

features.name: A/B testing
features.notes: Mixpanel runs experiments with statistics. OpenPanel can break any report down by a variant property, but has no experiment engine.

features.name: Feature flags
features.notes: Mixpanel includes feature flags on every plan (10 active on Free)

features.name: Session replay
features.notes: Mixpanel includes 10K replays a month on Free, 20K on Growth. OpenPanel replay is opt-in, masked by default and not metered.

features.name: Metric Trees
features.notes: Mixpanel's unique feature for mapping metrics to outcomes

features.name: Notifications/Alerts
features.notes: OpenPanel fires on events and completed funnels to Slack, Discord, email or a webhook. Mixpanel adds threshold and anomaly alerts.

features.name: EU data residency
features.notes: OpenPanel is EU-only; Mixpanel offers EU as an option

features.name: DPA available
features.notes: OpenPanel publishes its DPA at openpanel.dev/dpa

features.name: Warehouse connectors
features.notes: OpenPanel exports raw events to S3-compatible storage or GCS every minute; Mixpanel has native warehouse connectors

technical_comparison.title: Technical comparison
technical_comparison.intro: For developers evaluating analytics tools, here's how the SDKs and technical implementations compare.

items.label: SDK size (JS)
items.openpanel: About 3 KB gzipped; session replay loads as a separate script only when enabled
items.notes: OpenPanel's lighter SDK means faster page loads

items.label: Supported platforms
items.notes: Community SDKs exist for OpenPanel in PHP (Laravel) and Flutter. There is no Go SDK.

items.label: Self-hosted deployment
items.openpanel: Docker Compose (ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis), one-command install script

items.label: Database
items.notes: Self-hosters can query their own ClickHouse; there is no SQL editor in the dashboard

items.label: Autocapture
items.openpanel: Screen views, outgoing links and data-track attributes; everything else is an explicit call
items.notes: Mixpanel can automatically capture clicks, inputs, etc.

pricing.title: Pricing comparison
pricing.intro: OpenPanel is a flat monthly price for an event volume. Mixpanel is free up to 1M events and then priced in volume tiers.

openpanel.description: Flat monthly tiers by event volume: $2.50 for 5k events, $20 for 100k, $90 for 1M, $350 for 10M. 30-day free trial, then paid; there is no free tier. Self-hosting is free with unlimited events. Every feature on every tier.

competitor.description: Free up to 1M events a month, including 10K session replays and 10 active feature flags. Growth starts at $140/month for 1.5M events ($100 on yearly billing) and runs to 20M events at $2,289/month. Enterprise is custom. Group analytics and data pipelines are paid add-ons.

migration.title: Migrating from Mixpanel to OpenPanel
migration.intro: Switching from Mixpanel to OpenPanel is straightforward thanks to similar API patterns and our built-in import tool.

steps.title: Export your Mixpanel data
steps.description: Use Mixpanel's data export API to extract your historical events if you want to preserve them.

steps.title: Import into OpenPanel
steps.description: OpenPanel has a built-in Mixpanel importer: connect with a service account, your project id and a date range (US or EU residency) and it pulls the history in.

steps.title: Install the OpenPanel SDK
steps.description: Replace the Mixpanel SDK with OpenPanel's lightweight tracker. The API is similar, track(), identify(), and setGlobalProperties() work the same way.

steps.title: Update your event calls
steps.description: Most Mixpanel event calls translate directly. Review your implementation and update any Mixpanel-specific features.

steps.title: Verify and go live
steps.description: Run both tools in parallel briefly to validate data consistency, then switch fully to OpenPanel.

sdk_compatibility.notes: OpenPanel uses similar method names: track(), identify(), setGlobalProperties(). Most implementations translate with minimal changes.

historical_data.notes: Built-in Mixpanel importer in project settings: service account, project id, date range. Contact us for very large migrations.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about switching from Mixpanel to OpenPanel.

items.question: Does OpenPanel have all the features I use in Mixpanel?
items.answer: OpenPanel covers event tracking, funnels, retention, cohorts, user profiles, group analytics and session replay. It can compare variants by breaking a report down by a property, but has no experiment engine, no feature flags and no Metric Trees.

items.question: Can I import my historical Mixpanel data?
items.answer: Yes. OpenPanel has a built-in Mixpanel importer. Give it a service account, the project id and a date range, and your events are pulled in with their history.

items.question: How does pricing compare at scale?
items.answer: Below 1M events a month Mixpanel is free and OpenPanel Cloud is not. From there Mixpanel's first paid tier is $140 a month for 1.5M events ($100 on yearly billing), against $90 for 1M or $180 for 2.5M on OpenPanel. At 20M events Mixpanel lists $2,289 a month against $530. Self-hosting OpenPanel is free at any volume.

items.question: Is OpenPanel GDPR compliant?
items.answer: Yes. OpenPanel Cloud runs in Germany, tracking is cookie-free by default, and the data processing agreement is published at openpanel.dev/dpa.

items.question: Can I self-host OpenPanel?
items.answer: Yes. OpenPanel is open source (AGPL-3.0) and runs on Docker Compose with ClickHouse, Postgres and Redis. One install script sets it up. Self-hosting is free with unlimited events; releases arrive a month or two after Cloud.

items.question: How does the SDK size compare?
items.answer: OpenPanel's web script is about 3 KB gzipped. Mixpanel's browser SDK is over 20 KB. Session replay in OpenPanel loads as a separate script only when you enable it.

items.question: Does OpenPanel support mobile apps?
items.answer: Yes. OpenPanel has Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android) and React Native SDKs for event tracking. Session replay is web only; Mixpanel offers mobile replay on Enterprise.
